claims.text: Setting the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ (the Terraform state backend guide) exists and documents using Pulumi Cloud as a Terraform/OpenTofu state backend.
The self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service reads the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable, which specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` for the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API.
A separate domain for `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is not required: it can be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service.

The Terraform state backend guide (/docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/) uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the Terraform-compatible API domain in its `terraform login`/`tofu login` commands, Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, and `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
For a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name use the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value as the hostname.
